description: FP7 reviewed question set spanning all eight bundled document categories, including three deliberately unanswerable cases. Every answerable item was checked against its cited source and evidence.

questions.question: When does Fall 2026 registration begin in eServices?
questions.expected_answer: Fall 2026 registration begins Monday, March 23, 2026.
questions.expected_evidence: Monday, March 23, 2026 – Fall 2026 registration begins in eServices
questions.reviewer_notes: Distinguishes Fall 2026 from similar calendar documents.

questions.question: When does Spring 2026 registration begin?
questions.expected_answer: Spring 2026 registration begins Monday, October 20, 2025.
questions.expected_evidence: Monday, October 20, 2025 – Spring 2026 registration begins in eServices

questions.question: On what date does Summer 2026 open registration for visiting students begin?
questions.expected_answer: Summer 2026 open registration begins Monday, April 6, 2026.
questions.expected_evidence: Monday, April 6, 2026 – Summer 2026 OPEN (visiting students) registration begins in eServices

questions.question: How many transferable college-level semester credits make a student a transfer applicant?
questions.expected_answer: A student applies as a transfer applicant after attempting at least 16 transferable college-level semester credits.
questions.expected_evidence: Students who have attempted at least 16 transferable, college-level semester credits at another institution apply to Metro State as transfer students.

questions.question: What high school GPA qualifies a first-year applicant for automatic admission?
questions.expected_answer: Automatic first-year admission requires a cumulative high school GPA of 2.75 or higher.
questions.expected_evidence: Requires a cumulative high school GPA of 2.75 or higher

questions.question: Does the bookstore credit program give students free textbooks?
questions.expected_answer: No. It lets eligible students charge required materials to their student account, and they remain responsible for any balance not covered by aid.
questions.expected_evidence: Charges are applied to the student account and covered by financial aid once disbursed; students are responsible for any remaining balance not covered by aid.
accepted_answers: students are responsible for the remaining balance

questions.question: What expenses are included in Metro State's cost of attendance estimate?
questions.expected_answer: It includes tuition and mandatory fees, books and course materials, housing and food, transportation, personal expenses, and applicable loan fees.
questions.expected_evidence: Typical cost categories: Tuition and mandatory fees; Books and course materials; Housing and food; Transportation; Personal expenses; Loan fees (if applicable).
accepted_answers: tuition, books, housing, food, transportation, personal expenses, and loan fees

questions.question: What does last-dollar mean for the North Star Promise Scholarship?
questions.expected_answer: It covers remaining eligible tuition and fees after other federal and state grants have been applied.
questions.expected_evidence: It is a last-dollar scholarship, meaning it covers remaining tuition and fees after other federal and state grants have been applied.
accepted_answers: covers remaining tuition and fees after grants

questions.question: When does Return to Title IV review apply after a withdrawal?
questions.expected_answer: It applies when a student withdraws from all courses before completing more than 60 percent of the term.
questions.expected_evidence: Federal regulations require the university to review financial aid eligibility when a student withdraws before completing more than 60 percent of a term.
accepted_answers: before completing more than 60 percent of the term
withdraws from all courses before 60 percent

questions.question: What is the difference between graduation and commencement?
questions.expected_answer: Graduation officially confirms completion of degree requirements; commencement is an optional ceremony and does not itself confirm completion.
questions.expected_evidence: Graduation is the official confirmation that a student has completed all degree requirements. Commencement is a ceremonial event... Participation is optional and does not indicate that degree requirements are complete.
accepted_answers: graduation confirms degree completion; commencement is the ceremony

questions.question: When is Spring 2026 undergraduate and graduate commencement?
questions.expected_answer: Spring 2026 undergraduate and graduate commencement is Monday, May 4, 2026.
questions.expected_evidence: Monday, May 4, 2026 – Spring 2026 Undergraduate and Graduate Commencement

questions.question: Which grade is used in GPA calculations when a Metro State course is repeated?
questions.expected_answer: The most recent grade is used in the GPA calculation, although every attempt remains on the transcript.
questions.expected_evidence: The most recent grade is used in GPA calculations, although all attempts remain on the transcript.

questions.question: Does satisfactory academic progress affect financial aid eligibility?
questions.expected_answer: Yes. Students must meet GPA, completion-percentage, and maximum-timeframe standards to maintain financial aid eligibility.
questions.expected_evidence: SAP applies to financial aid eligibility. Students must meet GPA requirements, complete a minimum percentage of attempted credits, and finish their degree within the maximum timeframe.

questions.question: Which course delivery method has scheduled online video meetings?
questions.expected_answer: Online synchronous courses meet online at scheduled times using video conferencing.
questions.expected_evidence: Online Synchronous – Courses meet online at scheduled times using video conferencing.

questions.question: What should students check in eServices before their registration window opens?
questions.expected_answer: They should check for registration holds and resolve them before the window opens.
questions.expected_evidence: Check for registration holds in eServices and resolve them before your window opens.

questions.question: What are the Fall 2026 term dates?
questions.expected_answer: The Fall 2026 term runs from August 22 through December 13, 2026.
questions.expected_evidence: Fall 2026 Term Dates – August 22, 2026 to December 13, 2026

questions.question: What types of help do Metro State academic advisors provide?
questions.expected_answer: Advisors explain degree requirements, help plan schedules, review the Degree Audit Report, and help students stay on track for graduation.
questions.expected_evidence: Academic advisors help students understand degree requirements, plan course schedules, review their Degree Audit Report (DARs), and stay on track for graduation.
accepted_answers: degree requirements, schedules, degree audit, and graduation planning

questions.question: Where can students receive help with essays and research papers?
questions.expected_answer: The Writing Center helps students with essays, research papers, and other written assignments.
questions.expected_evidence: The Writing Center supports students with essays, research papers, and other written assignments.

questions.question: How much is the technology fee per credit?
questions.expected_answer: The technology fee is $14 per credit.
questions.expected_evidence: Technology Fee: $14 per credit.

questions.question: Which company administers Metro State's tuition payment plan?
questions.expected_answer: The tuition payment plan is offered through Nelnet Campus Commerce.
questions.expected_evidence: Metro State offers a tuition payment plan through Nelnet Campus Commerce.

questions.question: What is the general undergraduate tuition rate per credit for Fall 2025 through Summer 2026?
questions.expected_answer: The general undergraduate tuition rate is $302.84 per credit.
questions.expected_evidence: GENERAL RATES (Per Credit) Undergraduate: $302.84

questions.question: At what age can a Minnesota resident normally qualify for senior citizen tuition?
questions.expected_answer: A legal Minnesota resident normally qualifies at age 62 before the start of the term.
questions.expected_evidence: Must be 62 years old before the start of the term.
